rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Ethereum
positions.catalyst: ETHEREUM IS THE ONLY LIQUID MAJOR WHOSE INSTITUTIONAL BID IS STILL ACCELERATING WHILE ITS PRICE HAS NOT YET EXTENDED. Two things changed overnight and they point the same direction. (1) BITCOIN'S BID DECELERATED AND ITS BREAKOUT FAILED. BTC challenged $80,000 overnight and was rejected, slipping back to $77,034.59 on our canonical feed — a lower high and the FIRST NEGATIVE 24H PRINT of the entire advance (-0.94%). Spot BTC ETF net inflows fell to $307.5M on Aug 21 from $606.29M on Aug 20, a 49% deceleration in the single variable I underwrote yesterday. The thesis I bought BTC on was 'a fourth inflow day extends to a fifth at increasing size.' It extended, but at half size, and price could not hold the level. That is falsification, and I am acting on it rather than averaging into it. (2) ETH ETF FLOWS MADE A TEN-MONTH HIGH IN THE SAME WINDOW. Ether spot ETFs took $220.77M on Aug 20 — the LARGEST SINGLE DAY SINCE OCTOBER 28, 2025 — a fourth consecutive inflow day bringing the streak to $512.25M and August to roughly $534.2M, ETH's strongest month of 2026. BlackRock's ETHA led with $173M. So across the two ETF complexes the relative flow impulse INVERTED overnight: BTC's is halving off a 3.5-month high, ETH's is printing a 10-month high. That is the definition of a rotation with a dollar-denominated bid behind it rather than a chart pattern. ETH ALSO OUTPERFORMED BTC ON FRIDAY'S SESSION (roughly +8.1% vs BTC's +7.3%), which is unusual in a risk-on tape and is the signature of funds that were structurally UNDERWEIGHT ETH being forced to add. CRITICALLY, ETH HAS NOT GONE VERTICAL IN THE LAST 24 HOURS. FULL 24H RELATIVE STRENGTH, same-time-of-day vs yesterday's 10:52Z canonical pull: AAVE 111.86 -> 121.17 (+8.32%), XRP 1.3762 -> 1.487 (+8.05%), DOGE 0.08397 -> 0.08972 (+6.85%), ADA 0.21349 -> 0.22226 (+4.11%), DOT 0.887 -> 0.9186 (+3.56%), SOL 91.41 -> 92.96 (+1.70%), LINK 11.395 -> 11.542 (+1.29%), LTC 50.686 -> 51.209 (+1.03%), ETH 2395.10 -> 2410.94 (+0.66%), BTC 77767.55 -> 77034.59 (-0.94%), AVAX 7.589 -> 7.505 (-1.11%). ETH consolidated flat-to-up while BTC rolled over — it held the entire prior expansion without giving any of it back and without adding a stretched bar of its own. That combination (accelerating verified flows + no 24h extension) is the asymmetry this mandate asks for. Canonical dashboard proxy FRESH this run (asOf 2026-08-22T10:52:45Z): BTC 77034.59, ETH 2410.94, SOL 92.96, XRP 1.487, AAVE 121.17, LINK 11.542, LTC 51.209, AVAX 7.505, ADA 0.22226, DOT 0.9186, DOGE 0.08972.
positions.driver: Closed BTC at 77034.59 (canonical live, asOf 2026-08-22T10:52:45Z) vs entry 77767.55 for -113.62 (-0.94%). First losing day of this book's recent run and the lesson is narrow but real: I bought the liquid major precisely BECAUSE it had not gone parabolic, and that call was directionally right on risk — a -0.94% loss on a day when I explicitly flagged 'day three of a near-vertical advance' as the dominant risk is a cheap outcome, and it is exactly what the variance-reduction trade is supposed to deliver. The stop at 71,546 was never threatened. What I got wrong was the flow extrapolation: I underwrote a fifth consecutive ETF day at size and got a 49% deceleration plus a failed $80,000 test. So I am rotating on falsification, not on drawdown. I AM AGAIN DECLINING THE LEADERS, AND THIS TIME THE RECORD IS UNAMBIGUOUS. AAVE (+8.32%) and XRP (+8.05%) top the board. Yesterday I declined XRP at 1.3762 on the grounds that a 30% two-day vertical into resistance with 3% of room and 9% of air was the wrong shape — it then went up another 8%, so that specific call cost me relative return. I am still declining both, because the reasoning was about the SHAPE of the risk and the shape has only gotten worse: XRP is now four days into a ~40% advance with RSI deeply overbought and no fresh dated catalyst (the CLARITY Act vote cannot happen until lawmakers return in the fall — the White House meeting is already priced), and AAVE just printed its second consecutive near-10% session into the $108 200-day EMA with published momentum-exhaustion divergence flagged on Aug 21. This book has now lost money on AAVE once and has three separate instances of buying the prior session's leader and receiving a laggard. Paying the same tuition a fourth time on the same lesson would be indefensible. ETH TAKES THE SLOT ON THE FLOW INVERSION. It is 9th of 11 on raw 24h return, and that is precisely the qualification: the entire universe is 4 days into a melt-up, RSIs are stretched everywhere, and ETH is the only name with a LARGE, VERIFIED, ACCELERATING dollar bid ($220.77M, 10-month high, 4 straight days, $512M streak) that has NOT yet paid for it with a vertical bar. Every other name on the board is either extended (AAVE, XRP, DOGE, ADA), decelerating (BTC), or has no catalyst at all (SOL, LINK, LTC, AVAX, DOT). The mandate says favor liquid majors on low-edge days, and between the two majors the flow data now unambiguously favors ETH over BTC. Downside protection is genuine: ETH is the second-deepest book in crypto, so in a weekend flush it draws down materially less than the high-beta alts leading the tape, and the -8% stop at 2218.06 sits below yesterday's 2280.30 entry shelf — a routine retest of the prior consolidation does not take us out, but a loss of the whole two-day expansion does. RUNNERS-UP AND WHY NOT: BTC (-0.94%) — rejected at $80,000, flows halved, thesis falsified; holding it would be inertia. SOL (+1.70%) is the best-looking non-major on shape (quiet, not extended) but its Alpenglow catalyst is an October event and it has no institutional flow to point at inside a 24-hour window. DOGE (+6.85%) is pure retail beta with no catalyst and worst-in-class behavior in a flush. ADA (+4.11%) and DOT (+3.56%) are dominance-rotation noise — DOT was near the bottom two days ago, near the top yesterday, mid-pack today, which is rotation I cannot underwrite. AVAX (-1.11%) and LINK (+1.29%) and LTC (+1.03%) fail the screen with neither momentum nor catalyst.
positions.risks: THE FLOW INVERSION IS ONE DATA POINT AND IT IS BACKWARD-LOOKING. The $220.77M ETH print is Aug 20's number, reported after the fact, and I am extrapolating it into a fifth session — which is exactly the extrapolation that just failed me on BTC 24 hours ago. A 10-month-high inflow arriving on day three of a melt-up is as easily the underweight capitulating at a local top as it is the start of a sustained rotation. If ETH's Aug 21 flow prints materially lower the way BTC's did, the core of this thesis is gone within a day. CORRELATION MAKES THE ROTATION THESIS FRAGILE. ETH is not decoupled from BTC; realized correlation in crypto selloffs runs near 1. If BTC's failed $80,000 test is the top of this advance rather than a pause, ETH goes down with it and the 'accelerating ETF bid' will not matter over a 24-hour horizon. Everything I said about BTC's gap risk applies here too: ETH ran from roughly $1,900 to $2,410 in three sessions with thin intervening trade, so there is very little volume-based support beneath us and a full round-trip is more than -20% while the stop only protects the first 8% of it. WEEKEND LIQUIDITY IS THE SPECIFIC HAZARD TODAY. This is Saturday. Crypto books are thinnest on weekends, the ETF complex is CLOSED so the very bid I am underwriting cannot actually transact for two more days, and gap-through-stop slippage is materially more likely than on a weekday. I am buying an institutional-flow thesis on the two days institutions cannot participate — that is the sharpest internal contradiction in this trade and I want it on the record. THE MACRO DRIVER IS STILL AN ANNOUNCEMENT, NOT A FLOW. Treasury's buyback escalation does not begin until Sept 9; Bessent's 'could be more than $4 billion' remains guidance subject to walk-back, and the CLARITY Act cannot receive a vote until Congress returns in the fall. Nothing mechanical happens inside our window. The $40T debt milestone reads as debasement (bullish) or fiscal stress (risk-off) depending on the tape's mood, and live U.S.-Iran tension can flip from a crypto bid to a dollar-and-Treasuries bid without warning. THE SQUEEZE FUEL IS SPENT. Over $3B of crypto shorts were liquidated this week. Forced covering is non-recurring; four days in, offside positioning is largely cleared and the marginal buyer now has to be real money that cannot show up until Monday. RELATIVE UNDERPERFORMANCE IS THE LIKELIEST BENIGN FAILURE. If the melt-up continues into the weekend, AAVE and XRP will almost certainly capture more of it than ETH. I am again trading expected return for variance reduction, and I accept that it will look wrong on a continued risk-on tape — as it did yesterday. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION: a decisive loss of the 2280 shelf means the ETF-driven reclaim was squeeze artifact. Hard stop 2218.0648 (-8%, major-tier sizing) set beneath that shelf so a routine retest does not stop us out on noise while a genuine breakdown does.
